results.title: NAIMOS conducts 738 operations against illegal mining in four months
results.content: The National Anti-Illegal Mining Operations Secretariat (NAIMOS) says it conducted 738 operational activities between June 13 and September 30, 2026, as part of efforts to combat illegal mining and protect Ghana’s natural resources. Director of Operations at NAIMOS, Colonel K.S. Appiah, disclosed this during a media engagement, where he outlined the Secretariat’s operational achievements and plans to strengthen enforcement against illegal mining, popularly known as galamsey. According to him, the operations covered approximately 50,662 kilometres and included reconnaissance, mobile and riverine patrols, special operations and community engagement.

results.title: State appeals Court of Appeal ruling suspending Hanan’s trial over charge sheet dispute
results.content: The State has appealed to the Supreme Court against the Court of Appeal’s decision to suspend the criminal trial of former Buffer Stock CEO Hanan Aludiba and his wife, Faiza Seidu. Deputy Attorney-General and Minister for Justice, Dr Justice Srem-Sai, announced the appeal in a Facebook post on Thursday, October 22, 2026, saying it was filed on Wednesday, October 21. The appeal follows the Court of Appeal’s decision on Monday, October 19, to halt proceedings at the High Court pending the determination of Hanan Aludiba’s challenge to alleged defects in the charge sheet. Hanan Aludiba and his wife are standing trial on multiple charges, including stealing, defrauding by false pretences, wilfully causing financial loss to the Republic, using public office for profit, dishonestly receiving and money laundering.

results.title: Ghana Water rewards prompt-paying customers as complaints over unreliable supply persist
results.content: Ghana Water Limited’s Accra East Region is rewarding customers who consistently pay their water bills on time, even as some beneficiaries raise concerns about unreliable supply. The initiative, organised as part of Customer Service Month, involves visits to selected domestic, commercial and industrial customers who are being presented with customised gifts in recognition of their prompt payments. Chief Manager of the Accra East Region, Richard Appiah Otto, said the programme was intended to encourage payment discipline and help the company mobilise revenue to address operational challenges. “We have extreme difficulties in getting some customers to pay their water bills,” he said.

results.title: Protecting Ghana’s Students: Is the Time Right to revisit the case for Comprehensive Sexuality Education in our schools?
results.content: When students at Obuasi Senior High Technical School vented their anger on campus in August this year, damaging property and forcing the school to close, many of us saw only indiscipline. Look a little closer, and a more troubling picture appears: young people who, by several accounts, had been trying for months to be heard. At least 19 female students have accused their headmaster of sexual abuse over the past year, according to an investigation by journalist Manasseh Azure Awuni. The Ghana Education Service interdicted him on 14th October, and on 20th October, the Interior Minister told Parliament that he had been arrested and that DNA evidence was being pursued.

results.title: Daily Insight for CEOs: Preparing Leaders for 2027
results.content: The success of the organisation’s 2027 strategy will depend partly on whether its leaders have the skills, judgment, and capacity to execute it. CEOs must therefore assess leadership readiness before the new year begins. This means identifying capability gaps, preparing successors for critical positions, strengthening executive collaboration, and ensuring that managers can lead people through changing priorities and business demands.
